result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.trav_in_until()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Traverse inward node-by-node until stopping conditions are met. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L12679-L12880){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.trav_in_until( conditions, max_steps=30, exclude_unmatched=True, add_to_selection=False, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Inward traversal until a condition](/assets/graphs/trav-in-until.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Left: node C is selected in a seven-node directed graph whose nodes carry values; the condition is value at least 5. Right: walking backward against the arrows from C, the walk stops at A (value 6) on one branch and at F (value 7), via E, on the other, so A and F become the selection." width="100%"} From each currently selected node, walks backward along incoming edges (against the arrows) in breadth-first order and stops each branch at the first node that satisfies `conditions=`. Matching nodes are not expanded further, so anything upstream of them is never visited. Branches that never match keep going until they run out of incoming edges or until `max_steps=` hops have been taken. When the walk finishes, the node selection is replaced by the result. This is the mirror image of `trav_out_until()`. This is useful for: - tracing a node back to its nearest upstream source of a given kind (e.g., the originating account of a transaction chain, or the root cause in a dependency graph) - finding which ancestors first cross an attribute threshold - collecting everything between a node and those ancestors (with `add_to_selection=True, exclude_unmatched=False`) Things to keep in mind: - each starting node is traversed independently; the results are combined - a starting node that already satisfies the condition is kept as-is and not expanded - the method is meant for directed graphs; in an undirected graph, "incoming" neighbors are taken from the orientation in which edges were added, so the walk only follows edges back toward the node given as `source=` (use `trav_out_until()` to spread in all directions) - if no nodes are selected, the method does nothing - incoming neighbors are found by scanning the edge list for each visited node, and `conditions=` is a Python callable, so long walks on large graphs can be slow ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [conditions]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [callable]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A callable that receives a node ID (an `int`) and returns `True` when the walk should stop at that node. Node attributes can be read inside the callable, e.g., with `graph.get_node(node_id).attributes`. The callable is evaluated on the starting nodes too. [max_steps]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[30]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Maximum number of hops taken inward from each starting node. Default is `30`. When a branch reaches this depth without a match, the last frontier of unmatched nodes is what `exclude_unmatched=False` will keep (see below). [exclude_unmatched]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Whether nodes that do not satisfy `conditions=` may end up in the final selection. If `True` (the default), only matching nodes are selected, so a start node whose branches never match contributes nothing. If `False` and `add_to_selection=` is `False`, the deepest unmatched nodes reached (the frontier at `max_steps=`, or the level where the walk ran out of incoming edges) are selected alongside the matches. If `False` and `add_to_selection=` is `True`, every visited node is selected. [add_to_selection]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Whether to select the traversed path or just its endpoints. If `False` (the default), the selection becomes the matching nodes (plus the unmatched frontier when `exclude_unmatched=False`). If `True`, every node visited during the walk, including the starting nodes, is a candidate for selection; combined with the default `exclude_unmatched=True` that still filters down to the matching nodes, so pair it with `exclude_unmatched=False` to keep the whole traversed region. Note that the previous selection is always cleared first; only nodes visited by this walk can be selected afterward. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Self for method chaining. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Each node in this small directed graph carries a `value`. Starting at `D` and walking backward until a node has `value < 3` passes through `C` (value `3`) and stops at `B`. `A` also qualifies, but it lies upstream of `B`, so it is never reached: ::: {#6fa567ed .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph(directed=True) for label, value in [("A", 1), ("B", 2), ("C", 3), ("D", 9), ("E", 7), ("F", 8)]: graph.add_node(label=label, value=value) graph.add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("B", "E"), ("C", "D"), ("E", "F")]) def is_small(node_id): return graph.get_node(node_id).attributes["value"] < 3 start = graph.get_id_from_label("D") graph.select_nodes_by_id([start]).trav_in_until(is_small) sorted(graph.get_label_from_id(nid) for nid in graph.get_selected_node_ids()) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` ['B'] ``` ::: ::: Starting from both leaves, `D` and `F`, and looking for the root (`value == 1`) with `add_to_selection=True, exclude_unmatched=False` selects every ancestor visited on the way back, which here is the whole graph: ::: {#9809b9ee .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} def is_root(node_id): return graph.get_node(node_id).attributes["value"] == 1 leaves = [graph.get_id_from_label("D"), graph.get_id_from_label("F")] graph.clear_selection() graph.select_nodes_by_id(leaves) graph.trav_in_until(is_root, add_to_selection=True, exclude_unmatched=False) sorted(graph.get_label_from_id(nid) for nid in graph.get_selected_node_ids()) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` ['A', 'B', 'C', 'D', 'E', 'F'] ``` ::: ::: With the defaults instead, only the matching root `A` remains selected: ::: {#d80445d5 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph.clear_selection() graph.select_nodes_by_id(leaves) graph.trav_in_until(is_root) sorted(graph.get_label_from_id(nid) for nid in graph.get_selected_node_ids()) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` ['A'] ``` ::: :::
